tutorial.title: Run Testuary on the Toy
text: The adapter is ready for Testuary. A real Testuary run asks a language model for tests, which needs a model service and may cost money. This step plays a recorded Testuary run of the Toy instead. Every model answer and measurement comes from the recording, and the playback runs no tool and contacts no service.
The run was recorded with this tutorial's prepared adapter, so it shows the prepared solution even where you kept your own version. Its records go to testuary-run in this directory.

For a real run of your own language, name the file langadapter new-language writes in [main] extensions of the project's settings file, and select the language: testuary --languages <name> with your project and model.
tutorial.install: Testuary is a separate package: python -m pip install testuary

families.improves: keeps generated suites that fail to load, repaired
families.fallback: a generated suite that does not load is discarded

families.improves: keeps generated suites whose only fault is an import that does not resolve
families.fallback: a generated suite with an unresolvable import does not load and is discarded

families.improves: keeps suites with a local syntax error, repaired
families.fallback: a suite that does not parse is discarded

families.improves: keeps whole-file skips from hiding the tests of a suite
families.fallback: whole-file skips stay, and a suite without a passing test is rejected

families.improves: names in the starter prompt the import line a test needs, or that it needs none
families.fallback: the starter prompt asks the model to follow the language's import conventions

families.improves: reduces suites while keeping every mutant kill
families.fallback: the suite reductions that must keep every kill are skipped

families.improves: combines a phase's candidate suites into one
families.fallback: the better single candidate is kept, by mutation score, then branch coverage, then line coverage, then the timing tie-break

families.improves: reduces suites to the tests that add coverage or kills
families.fallback: suite reduction is skipped and each phase chooses among unreduced suites. Each starter suite is scored on its own measurements

families.improves: finds the tests whose run warns of leaked state, such as an unawaited coroutine: the starter suites' cleanup removes them, and a loop counts their passing run as failing
families.fallback: such tests are neither removed nor counted as failing

families.improves: runs a suite the way a user would run it, as the normal run of a language whose runs as delivered take a session seed and for the reverse-order note
families.fallback: the normal run is the language's own test run, and the reverse-order note is off

families.improves: rejects generated tests that read the implementation
tells equal suites apart by their run time and records it
families.fallback: the timing tie-break is off, the input order decides, and no run time is recorded

families.improves: notes runtime versions and refuses unsupported ones
families.fallback: every runtime version is reported as untested
suites run on this machine only

families.improves: reports sizes and complexity in Finishing
